newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps tick upwards, but only moderately.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps tick upwards, but only moderately.

text.p: European oil swaps were broadly firmer on Thursday with Brent CFDs gaining a few cents, gasoline stronger by 50 cents or so and along with naphtha and fuel fairly steady.
Screen crude lost ground as the market put a question mark over OPEC'S talk of firmer commitment on quota leakage. Dealers were cautious about how OPEC was going to enforce quota compliance.

Brent CFDs gained a few cents with June 30-July 4 hovering around -37 cents against August Brent from -40 cents on Wednesday with July 7-11 pegged flat after a morning CFD trade at -35 cents. July 14-18 was put at -35 cents while July 21-25 was assessed at -30 cents, but no deals were heard on these dates.
Heavy fuel swaps attracted attention around 4Q and 1Q98 and dealers commented on the steepening contango. One said storage companies might start to get active if the contango went another $1 or so.
"End-users still have hedging to do and bearish talk will encourage buying," said one dealer.
4Q traded a couple of times at $91.50 and also at $92.00 and the contango steepened into 1Q98 which traded at $95.50. 4Q to 1Q98 traded at $3.50.
Closer in saw high sulphur swaps trading at $82.25 for July, $83.25 for July, $84.25 for August and $85 for September.

Low sulphur swaps were a touch firmer from Wednesday by $1 or so, but July swaps were still backwardated against wet barrels. August and September were fairly flat against July with September showing a $1 contango.
Gasoline swaps initially gained in the morning rising by up to $3, but spent the afternoon drifting back down. July, August and September were all valued at $180.00, about $1 higher than Wednesday.
Naphtha swaps were stable with July heard trading at $174.00 and $174.50 for July, but the market was very slow with several key players out of the market due to a function.
